frameworkName: OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications
licenseNote: OWASP content is available under Creative Commons licensing. Summaries below are original interpretive content written for this application, not reproductions of OWASP's text.
demonstrationSubsetDisclaimer: This is an illustrative subset for portfolio demonstration purposes, not full framework coverage.

controls.title: Prompt injection defenses
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to detect or mitigate prompt injection attacks, where crafted input causes the LLM to ignore its intended instructions.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask for evidence of actual adversarial testing against prompt injection, not just a general statement of input validation.

controls.title: Insecure output handling
controls.summary: LLM outputs are treated as untrusted input when passed to downstream systems (e.g. not directly executed as code or rendered unsanitized in a browser).
controls.validationGuidance: This is especially important for agentic systems where the LLM's output can trigger actions - confirm outputs are validated before use.

controls.title: Training data poisoning controls
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to verify the integrity and provenance of data used to train or fine-tune models, reducing risk of intentional poisoning.
controls.validationGuidance: Most relevant for vendors that fine-tune models on customer or third-party data - lower priority for vendors using unmodified foundation models.

controls.title: Model denial of service protections
controls.summary: The vendor has rate limiting or resource controls to prevent resource-exhaustion attacks against LLM inference endpoints.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for evidence of actual rate limiting configuration, not just a stated intention to have it.

controls.title: Supply chain security for models and plugins
controls.summary: The vendor verifies the provenance and integrity of third-party models, embeddings, or plugins integrated into its AI system.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask specifically about how third-party model weights or plugin code are vetted before integration.

controls.title: Sensitive information disclosure prevention
controls.summary: Controls exist to prevent the LLM from revealing sensitive information it may have been exposed to during training or in context, such as PII or proprietary data.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for output filtering or redaction mechanisms specifically, since this is a known and common failure mode for LLMs.

controls.title: Excessive agency limitations
controls.summary: Where the LLM can take autonomous actions (e.g. calling tools or APIs), its permissions are scoped to the minimum necessary rather than broad system access.
controls.validationGuidance: This is critical for agentic AI systems - confirm the LLM cannot take high-impact actions (e.g. financial transactions, data deletion) without human confirmation.

controls.title: System prompt leakage protections
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to reduce the risk of the system prompt or internal instructions being extracted by an end user.
controls.validationGuidance: Ask whether the system prompt contains sensitive logic or secrets that would matter if exposed - if not, this control is lower priority.

controls.title: Overreliance and output validation guidance for end users
controls.summary: The vendor provides guidance or interface cues that discourage end users from treating LLM outputs as authoritative without verification.
controls.validationGuidance: Look for this especially in high-stakes use cases (medical, legal, financial guidance) where overreliance carries real consequences.

controls.title: Model theft and extraction protections
controls.summary: The vendor has controls to reduce the risk of model weights or proprietary fine-tuning being extracted through repeated querying or direct access.
controls.validationGuidance: More relevant for vendors who have invested in proprietary fine-tuning - lower priority for those using unmodified third-party APIs.
